topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: The defocused reflector's unique beam pattern minimizes defocusing effects on outer feed elements by bending the feed array to bring the outer elements closer to the position of the outer feed elements of the conventional reflector. This reduces defocusing on these elements, leading to a more efficient signal path and interaction with the receiving antenna. This robustness enhances link budget margins and SNR performance.
